history.summary: IDENTITY CONFIRMED: the famous Ghaghar Buri Kali temple of Asansol — a small shrine to Goddess Kali on the bank of the Nunia rivulet by the NH-19 bypass at Kalipahari/Domohani, Asansol, described on Wikipedia as the oldest temple of the city. Legend: a marriage procession (baraat) could not cross the Nunia rivulet in spate; it worshipped the deity, the waters subsided, and it crossed safely — but the king forgot his promise of two goats, and the goddess cursed the procession, which perished in the water (old locals say the drowned baraat is still visible; foam on the rivulet is taken as proof). Folk origin: Ghaghrabudi ('the old woman in a skirt', Bengali ghaṣhra) was a tribal ancestor goddess dwelling in egg-shaped stones under a tree on the Nunia bank; a 1956 flood uprooted the tree and revealed her stones, and she appeared to the depressed brahmin Kangal Chakravarti as an old woman in a ghaghra, commanding worship in the form of the stones — the deity was then brahmanised as Ghaghrachandi and later Ghaghradevi. Worship is held every Tuesday and Saturday; a country fair is held on 15 January each year; animal sacrifice is part of worship.

name: Ghaghar Buri Temple
town_description: Asansol, the 'City of Brotherhood', is a major industrial and coal-mining city in Paschim Bardhaman district, West Bengal — one of the largest urban centres of the state and a historic railway hub on the Howrah-Delhi route. The Ghaghar Buri temple stands on the Nunia rivulet beside the NH-19 bypass in the Kalipahari/Domohani area of the city.
